subject: MSA / Order Form — inspection fallback, evidence cadence, and pen-test sequencing
messages:
From: Claire Huang <c.huang@luminahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: LuminaHealth Legal <legal@luminahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify inspection rights / pen-test window and evidence cadence

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the MSA draft. A couple of items from our security and procurement teams we need clarity on before we can move to legal redlines:

- Pen test scope and timing: our security team needs to know whether you will allow a vendor-led pen test against staging or if Redwood will perform tests and provide results. We prefer a vendor test against staging with ephemeral access.
- Evidence cadence for SOC 2 and operational assertions: we typically ask for a sampling cadence (weekly snapshots + quarterly roll-up) and a final handback artifact set.
- Fallback & non-production data handling: what happens if staged testing isn’t feasible (air-gapped tenants, HIPAA constraints)?

I attached our audit checklist and marked the sections that triggered the questions. Can you map how Redwood typically handles these items (redline language and operational handoff)?

We’re aiming to finalize the orders and signatures by the end of the month — appreciate a plan we can include with the MSA redlines.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Huang
Security Program Manager
LuminaHealth

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify inspection rights / pen-test window and evidence cadence

Hi Claire —

Thanks — and appreciate the checklist. Below is a concise proposal that maps to each of your asks; I’ve also attached an editable redline (redline_security_exhibit_v2.docx) and an evidence mapping workbook (evidence_mapping_lumina.xlsx) so you and legal can see exact clause language and artifacts.

Proposal (high-level):
1) SOC 2 / attestation: Redwood will provide our most recent SOC 2 Type II report and a SOC attestation summary as part of onboarding. Access will be via a secure portal link (attached in evidence mapping).

2) Pen-test sequencing and scope:
   - Primary path: Lumina’s approved third-party vendor may run non-destructive tests against a staging environment we provision for the engagement (ephemeral staging identical to production topology where feasible).
   - Window & notice: typical window is a 10 business day testing window with a 5 business day pre-notice and a post-test review call within 3 business days.
   - Constraints: testing must be non-disruptive; exfiltration of production PII is prohibited; Redwood will provide scoped data-masking guidance.

3) Evidence cadence and handback:
   - Weekly artifacts: during the engagement we’ll share weekly snapshot packs (logs, SRs, config exports) for the test scope; final handback includes the pen-test report (redacted as needed), test logs, and a remediation timeline.
   - If staging access is restricted, Redwood will run the agreed test plan internally and provide the same artifact set plus a recorded walkthrough.

4) Fallbacks & escalation:
   - If vendor staging access cannot be provided due to regulatory constraints, we offer: (a) an internal RDC-executed test with artifact handback, or (b) a recorded run and signed affidavit describing test steps and findings.

5) Frequency & limits: Proposed contractual language limits full external vendor inspections to 2 per 12-month period and allows additional inspections only by mutual written agreement.

Next steps: Karthik — can legal weigh in on the inspection frequency cap and the suggested affidavit fallback? Monica — can you confirm the operational runbook and who will own ephemeral access provisioning? Claire — if this aligns, we can circulate redline_security_exhibit_v2 and update the order form for signatures.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Manager — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify inspection rights / pen-test window and evidence cadence

Soojin / Claire —

Quick legal read and suggested adjustments: overall approach is reasonable, our main asks are to make the right to inspect operationally bounded and to protect Redwood and its subprocessors from open-ended obligations. Specifics:

- Frequency cap: I support limiting vendor-led inspections to 2 per 12 months, but suggest adding language that emergency or regulatory inspections can be requested with reasonable proof and a good-faith review (we can capture an SLA for turnaround).

- Non-disruption & exfiltration: Add explicit non-disruption covenant for testers and a prohibition on active exploitation of vulnerabilities that materially impact the environment (we can include a ‘safe-ops’ testing boundary).

- Data handling & redaction: If test artifacts contain sensitive customer data, Redwood may redact or mask values, and will provide a summary of the raw artifact access method in a secure repository for agreed reviewers.

- Affidavit fallback: Acceptable, but we should require a Redwood-signed attestation and scope matrix to ensure parity with vendor results.

I’ve put inline suggested clause text into the redline (I created redline_security_exhibit_v3.docx). If Claire is good with this direction, we can finalize language and attach it to the order form as an exhibit; I’ll also prepare a one-paragraph executive summary for procurement to keep the signature path smooth.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify inspection rights / pen-test window and evidence cadence

Thanks — this is helpful and mostly aligns with Lumina’s needs. A few follow-ups before we finalize:

1) Can we shift the testing window to 2 full calendar weeks instead of 10 business days? That gives our vendors a little more scheduling flexibility.
2) We’re OK with the 2-per-year cap if emergency inspections are described and preserved.
3) For the affidavit fallback, we’d like the attestations to include a short scope checklist (hostnames, attack surface, tools used) to verify parity with a vendor-run test.

If you can accept (1) and include the checklist requirement for the affidavit, we’ll approve the exhibit language and move to procurement to get the order form signed. Please send the updated exhibit and I’ll confirm a kickoff call availability — we’re free on week of 12/21 for a 30–45 minute call.

Claire
